newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index falls 1.42 pct at close.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index falls 1.42 pct at close.

text.p: The Philippine equities market closed in negative territory for the fifth straight day on Friday weighed down by Wall Street's jitters, traders said.
"There's foreign bearishness and most investors feel there's a high correlation between the U.S. and the Philippine market," said Raymond Garcia, president at Diversified Securities.
The main index closed 44.18 points down, or 1.42 percent, at 3,060.59.
"Investors would like to be liquid rather than be in a market where direction is not clear," said Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asiamerit Securities.
Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor Hagedorn Securities Inc, said investors, especially foreigners, opted to sell ahead of the release of U.S. employment data later on Friday.
Among the biggest losers was San Miguel Corp B shares which closed nine pesos lower, 10 percent, at 81 pesos. San Miguel A, on the other hand, ended steady at 55 pesos.

"Some people are raising questions on the deal between San Miguel and Coca-Cola Amatil but since other B shares are down and San Miguel A shares ended unchanged, then it's a combination of both the bearishness of the market and concerns on the deal," Garcia said.
San Miguel has announced its plans to merge its Coke bottling unit with Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd, a deal company officials said would bring global growth opportunities for San Miguel.
The market was halted shortly after the session started due to a power failure. Trading resumed just 30 minutes before the close of trade.
Value turnover was substantial at 2.3 billion pesos considering the temporary stoppage of trading.
Traders said attention will continue to be riveted on the Dow, which is expected to dictate the market's pace next week.
